They make superficial diagnoses and force you to file an insurance claim without even checking the problem first. I took my Lexus RX450h+ in because it wasn't handling properly. They told me I'd hit something and bent a rim, which isn't true, but then they checked and found no rims were bent.

After 19 days without my car, they've replaced parts of the rear suspension—which ones? I have no idea since they won't give me any more information—and two tires, but it's still not handling properly. They don't explain the cause; they just say it "isn't handling right." A surreal situation for a car worth over €90,000.

Lexus Spain, KINTO, and the dealership are ignoring my complaints. I can't return the car or stop making payments without breaching the contract. The lease was arranged and signed at this dealership, but now they're trying to distance themselves from KINTO.

After 19 days, a wrong diagnosis, a repair that doesn't solve the problem, and no explanation, my only options are to get it inspected by an independent professional and consider legal action. Be very cautious with this dealership, Lexus Spain and KINTO.

PS: TO LEXUS'S RESPONSE: Just empty words. I wrote to that email address 15 days ago, before my review, and no, I haven't received any response. You only respond to public inquiries.

I repeat, a single absence and they make her pay.

My level of indignation is high, and I hereby state this.

Overrated and not as international as advertised

I visited Hello Club Mallorca after seeing several recommendations describing it as an international club, and unfortunately, my experience did not live up to those expectations.

The venue itself is fairly typical and, in my opinion, does not offer anything particularly distinctive compared with many other clubs. Having experienced nightlife in Berlin, I would describe Hello Club as a fairly standard club rather than a genuinely international nightlife destination.

What disappointed me most was the lack of an international atmosphere. Despite being in a major tourist destination like Mallorca and being promoted/recommended as an international club, communication was predominantly in German or Spanish. As an international visitor, I found it surprisingly difficult to communicate in English. Even basic interactions felt unnecessarily challenging, and there was little effort to accommodate English-speaking guests.

For a club located in such a multicultural and tourist-heavy destination, I would expect a more inclusive environment where English is reasonably accessible alongside Spanish and German. An international club should ideally feel welcoming to visitors from different countries, not make them feel like outsiders because they do not speak the local languages.

The music, atmosphere, service, and overall experience were fairly ordinary and did not justify the reputation or recommendations I had seen beforehand.

If you are specifically looking for a truly international nightlife experience in Mallorca, I would suggest managing your expectations before visiting. Based on my experience, I would not consider this a must-visit destination simply because it is described as an “international club.”

For me, the experience was fairly average and not worth going out of my way for.

I'm giving it one star because I can't give less.

I've been contacting the City Hall for three months, filing complaints and official requests, asking for something as basic as the pruning and maintenance of a tree right outside my garage. It's a danger to pedestrians.

I've even spoken directly with the mayor, Pilar, and the response I get is that I need a curbside pickup because, according to her, if I cross the street, the neighbors could report me since it's public property. (And she's perfectly happy with that.)

But a curbside pickup is one thing, and maintaining a tree on public property is quite another, which is precisely what I've been requesting for months. I don't understand what the two have to do with each other.

Meanwhile, the Bartodano residential area has a feeling of neglect and lack of maintenance that we residents have been suffering from for some time.

What's most disappointing isn't just that a problem takes so long to resolve, but having to insist repeatedly, submit requests and complaints, and feeling like no one is taking responsibility for providing a solution.

I hope the City Council starts addressing residents' complaints and, above all, takes action instead of simply making excuses.

I am leaving this review to express my profound dissatisfaction with the service I received from the after-sales department and the workshop at Sarauto.

Last Tuesday, my vehicle was flooded in Montcada i Reixac. As it is a leased vehicle, it was taken to this workshop on Wednesday. Since then, the handling has been appalling:
Complete lack of communication: The workshop hasn't even contacted me to inform me about the vehicle's condition or the procedure.

Lack of information on the next steps: The only people I've been able to speak with are Carolina (reception) and Xavier (sales). Although they have answered my calls, no one at the dealership can give me a clear answer or guide me on the procedures or the next steps.

Lack of customer protection: The only response from reception is that they have to wait for the insurance adjuster to visit. Meanwhile, I find myself completely without assistance, without a replacement car (as it's not included in the leasing policy), and still paying my monthly lease installment without receiving any guidance on what will happen if the vehicle is declared a total loss.

It's unacceptable that an official after-sales service leaves a customer in limbo in an urgent and critical situation. I expect management to take steps to improve internal coordination and customer service.
After waiting in the store for more than half an hour and seeing several dealership workers pass me by pretending they weren't there, I had to leave without being served.

one_star_reviews.text: The staff's attention is very poor; when you're shopping, it's uncomfortable because the stockers have the aisles full. Almost always, when queuing at the checkout, the staff have priority to go ahead with the excuse that they are going to lunch and don't have time. They have a lot to improve.

Ticket for the butcher shop at 11:47, 5 people were serving at that moment, with 41 people ahead of me according to the ticket. At one point, 3 of the staff left, the two who were serving were chatting amongst themselves, laughing. Two more appeared, but instead of moving up the queue, they started restocking, talking amongst themselves. I had to repeat myself twice what I wanted because they didn't understand. Knowing how much demand there is in this place, they should hire more staff who are actually willing to work and serve the customers. They save their chatter for when they're having a coffee! So, for just 4 things I bought, I paid over €160 just at the butcher shop, waiting until 13:29, by which time the 41 tickets ahead of me had been taken, skipping every 3-4 numbers because people get tired and leave!

On top of everything, I got stuck with Belen, who, if you say anything to her, turns away and talks to her colleague, gives you dirty looks, is unenthusiastic and very rude!

This is my second time here. The first time I didn't have much time to explore, but today I wanted to take a closer look.
Since I didn't buy anything because there were so many people waiting to pay and only two registers open, I asked where I could leave without making a purchase.
An employee told me to leave through a register. Since the registers were full and I wasn't going to wait, a woman who was also leaving left through a closed register, and I followed her.
I heard the employee from before start yelling at me that I couldn't leave that way, that I had to leave through a register with a cashier to check that I wasn't taking anything without paying.
In other words, there's no way out without a purchase; they force you to leave through a register and wait in line to get out, they insult you by implying you're stealing, and they yell at you as if you were deaf or stupid.

I believe everyone has the right to work, but I also believe that people who work with the public should have a minimum level of courtesy, not yell at people, and have some empathy. This employee is incredibly rude, and this company should have a designated exit without purchases and a security guard monitoring it to prevent theft, as all serious and responsible businesses do. Given this behavior, I certainly wouldn't recommend anyone visit, and I definitely don't think I'll be returning.

one_star_reviews.text: Beware of thieves, even though you have purchased insurance, they force you to buy additional insurance that is several times more expensive, scaring you with repair costs, damages, etc. I do not recommend it.

They have failed to refund the €350 deposit for the vehicle we returned on September 5th—for which they confirmed there was no damage—despite the maximum 28-day period having already passed. During this time, I emailed the Budget office at Tenerife North and received an automated reply stating that my request was being processed, yet no action has been taken. I also submitted a request via Booking to resolve the issue, but there has been no progress. I demand the immediate refund of my deposit.

Budget Tenerife South was the worst car rental experience I've ever had.

1. The agency isn't at the airport. You have to take a shuttle, and this isn't clearly indicated when you book.

2. There are no signs to help you find them. No signs at all, neither for the shuttle nor for the agency. You just wander around with your luggage.

3. An agency that isn't even at the airport is a bad sign from the start, and what follows confirms it.
When you finally arrive at their office, the trap is sprung. They force you to take out their in-house insurance, which is outrageously expensive. If you refuse it because you already purchased insurance online when you booked, they threaten you: the slightest scratch of 1 cm will cost you €2,500, per scratch! And they hold a €16,000 deposit for a vehicle that's probably already well depreciated and covered by their own insurance. The result: unbearable sales pressure, a real feeling of being ripped off, and a ruined start to the vacation.

My advice: don't book online with them. Rent directly on arrival. For me, the best agency is Hertz.

TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE. I recommend renting from any other company, even if it's a bit more expensive, to avoid waiting and unpleasant surprises.

When we went to pick up the car, we had to wait quite a while to be attended to, and the employee gave us incorrect directions to the vehicle.

And upon delivery, they inspected it, saying everything was fine, and then 5 hours later I received an email demanding €292 of the deposit back for an alleged scratch on the bumper, without providing any proof, even though they had told me in my presence when they received the car that everything was fine and there were no issues. I have filed a complaint, and if they don't refund it, I will report them.

In short, APPALLING.

Unclear charges, pressured insurance sale, and a car that did not match the booking.

The booking was made through Booking for an Audi Q3 with an automatic transmission and insurance included. However, when we arrived, we were initially given a lower-class vehicle with a manual transmission. After we asked to receive a car matching our booking, the employee said they would “make an exception” and found an automatic vehicle. Nevertheless, it was still a lower-class car than the Audi Q3 we had booked.

During the rental process, additional insurance was added. The employee was unable to clearly explain how it differed from the insurance included in the Booking.com reservation or why it was necessary to purchase it separately. As a result, the cost of the rental increased significantly.

The most unpleasant issue happened after we returned the car. The amount quoted and charged at the desk turned out not to be final: an additional payment was taken later. The rental agreement divides the total amount into two payments, but does not clearly state why the second payment was charged or which service it relates to. Fuel had been paid for in advance, and there were no damages, fines, or other issues when the vehicle was returned. We only learned about the additional charge afterwards.

In addition, because the vehicle was changed, we were initially given a rental agreement for the wrong car. We had to request the correct agreement separately through customer support instead of receiving it at the desk when the rental was arranged.

In the end, instead of a straightforward rental based on a prepaid booking, we faced long queues, a car below the booked category, unclear additional insurance, an incorrect rental agreement, and unexplained charges after the return. The rental ultimately cost far more than expected. A very disappointing experience — I would not recommend this company to anyone who values transparent pricing and receiving the vehicle they booked.

one_star_reviews.text: Customer service for online purchases was terrible and offered no solutions. I will never shop online again.

Very disappointed with the service I received.

On August 31st, I bought a Polti iron from the El Corte Inglés website for €219. I don't usually buy online, as I always prefer to go to the store in person, but on this occasion, I had a fall, broke my ankle, and had surgery, so I couldn't go to the store. My daughter made the purchase in my name because I needed the iron.

When I received the product, I opened the box to see it and realized it wasn't the model I actually wanted. I wanted the higher-end model and was even willing to pay €100 more for it. The iron I bought is completely brand new and unused.

Furthermore, El Corte Inglés called me twice. At the time, I was in the hospital and couldn't answer the calls. On Monday, they called me again to offer me insurance, something I didn't quite understand at the time.

Today I finally went in person to the El Corte Inglés store on Avenida de Francia, thinking I could resolve the issue, and I was greatly disappointed to discover that they told me the return period was 15 days, not 30, and that, moreover, because the box was damaged, they couldn't accept the return.

I understand that there are return policies, but I believe that in circumstances like mine, they could have been a little more understanding and tried to find a solution. Especially since the product is brand new and unused, and I was even willing to exchange it for a higher-end model, paying the difference.

I found the service I received particularly unpleasant. For €219, and being a customer who usually buys directly in-store, I expected better treatment and more support in resolving the problem.

I am leaving El Corte Inglés very disappointed, not because of the product's quality, but because of the service I received and their unwillingness to find a solution.

one_star_reviews.text: The bus just got off in Torrent and the driver won't open the door for me, leaving me with it slammed in my face. A nasty driver, making me late for work because of him. 170 stop 3917

Hello, good afternoon. I'm going to tell you what happened to me today. It's surreal but true. I was about to catch a Fernanbus 106 towards the airport, which already costs €5, around 4 pm. One arrived at the roundabout by the tobacconist on Calle Mayor. There were others on the steps in front and behind, and the driver told me to get on, which I refused. I went to Concordia, in front of Mercadona, desperate. Around 5:07 pm, another bus arrived, half full. I let the four people on, and to my surprise, he closed the doors on me. I only managed to pull my hands away because he started driving off, closing the doors, and other people told him there was a problem. He didn't care. Well, I know exactly what I'm talking about because I'm a bus driver, and this is shameful.

Today, with the Red Alert in place, the students left a little earlier, anxious about the situation. They took the 170 bus in front of the Veles & Vent school to get home faster. But the driver couldn't think of anything better to do than drop them off two stops later. And there I was, waiting for my daughter at the stop closest to home. I think it's outrageous and shows a lack of empathy and responsibility. They need to take a closer look at who they put in front of those buses.

The driver showed a complete lack of sensitivity. He's an elderly man who will probably face the same treatment soon. Today, my 82-year-old mother and my 6-year-old son boarded the bus after school, thinking it was the local bus. Without saying a word or explaining anything, the driver stopped the bus and made them get off. He's an elderly person who can barely hear. Good manners are disappearing these days. On top of that, he didn't even bother to collect the fare or anything; he just made them get off. It's a disgrace.

Honestly, one of the worst agencies in the city. At least, that's how it was with the agent named Catalina. There was zero communication from her. She was supposed to act as an intermediary between landlords and tenants, but that wasn't the case. We had to discuss everything directly with the landlords (thankfully, they did respond and address our needs). The last straw was when our lease ended. On June 29, 2026, we signed the vacating papers and returned the keys to the apartment. From that day forward, we were no longer responsible for paying the utilities (water, electricity, and gas) for the apartment (Catalina, the real estate agent, said she would take care of canceling our service with the utility company). Well, days later, on July 12, 2026, they notified us that they had just canceled our service. Of course, we received utility bills for those days when we were no longer living in the apartment. We told Catalina about it, and she took a while to respond, initially saying that YES, it was our responsibility to pay. We carefully reviewed the invoices we received from those days and reiterated that we weren't responsible for those payments, so we told her again. Her response was that she would review it again and get back to us. Obviously, after several days, we had to contact her again to get an answer. This time, she told us that yes, we were right and those payments weren't our responsibility, and that she would speak with the owners so they would take over the payments (all of this happened between mid- and late July 2026). It's now early October, and they're still charging our bank account (we obviously returned the invoice to avoid being charged since it wasn't our responsibility). This time, we sent her a message clearly expressing our dissatisfaction. Her response? To read the message and not reply at all. Faced with this situation, we decided to speak directly to the owners, who were unaware of these payments that were not our responsibility. Catalina had not spoken to the owners as she claimed. As I mentioned before, this woman never acted as a mediator; she only focused on collecting our money. Thanks to the owners, we will be able to resolve this issue once and for all. I don't know if this is typical of the company, but if you encounter Catalina, be aware that she will not be of any help.

I'm editing my review again because your response is even more pathetic than your inaction, implying in your writing that I misused an armchair that's only TWO MONTHS old. Do you think I've been jumping on it or throwing myself down the stairs with it? It's a RELAXING armchair, you hear? A relaxing armchair for my own use and enjoyment, for an adult of average height and weight who comes home from work and wants to sit in it.

I don't want your lousy repair or your stupid report. The quality of your products is TERRIBLE, and I want my money back because I promise I won't stop until I get it.

Regarding the store where I bought it, Factory del Mueble in Utrera also got their share of the blame. They're passing the buck just like you and blaming you, just as you blame them, for their responsibility to the customer. So that's where we are: a brand fighting with the store to see who jumps ship first.

HERE'S MY INITIAL REVIEW: A lot of hype, but terrible quality, plus appalling and rude customer service.

A few months ago, we bought an Amira reclining armchair and a corner sofa for almost €4,000.
After two months of use, the reclining sofa started to become unstable laterally when open, tipping over completely to the point where you would fall over, making it impossible to sit in.

It feels more like a rocking chair than a recliner.
After several weeks of waiting for a repair, they took it away after only two months, leaving it at the factory for over a month before supposedly returning it repaired.
After another two months of use, the same problem has returned: the metal frame seems too small for the size of the sofa.

I'm writing to the factory again to request a refund, as I don't want a sofa with a design flaw, or whatever they want to call it. Consumer law protects me since a previous repair has already been carried out, so I demand the termination of the contract and a refund of the €923 I paid.

The factory's response was rude, impolite, and inappropriate. They stated they would proceed with the repair again but threatened to "review the protocol to check if the sofa has been used properly."

I will definitely file complaints with the consumer protection agency and the OCU (Spanish Consumer Organization) if they don't terminate the contract and refund my money. And of course, I will NEVER buy from this company again, a company that boasts about quality when it's all name and facade.

Looks the part, but a very disappointing steak
We visited La Cascada expecting a delicious steak. The restaurant looks lovely, has a nice atmosphere and an impressive meat display, but unfortunately the meal did not live up to that promise.
I ordered the €40 speciality Txogitxu rib-eye, cooked medium. It arrived rare, with hard, chewy fat rather than the soft, buttery texture I expected. Much of the steak was unpleasant to eat, and it was quite possibly the worst steak I have ever had—especially disappointing at that price. We also waited around 20 minutes for a drink.
After raising the issue with two members of the waiting staff, we eventually spoke to the manager, who confirmed he had seen my returned plate. Roughly half the steak was left, including the hard fat and meat I had been unable to eat. His response that other customers love their food felt dismissive of our experience.
They deducted €20 from the bill, which I appreciate, but it did not make up for such a disappointing meal or the fact my partners meal was also awful.  Another diner nearby also told us he wasn’t happy with his steak, although he chose not to complain.
A lovely setting, but based on our visit, the steak quality and handling of our complaint fell well short of expectations. We would not return or reccomend.

I formally requested the cancellation of a treatment within the 30-day period stipulated in my contract. Since then, I have sent emails, WhatsApp messages, made several calls, and visited the clinic in person on several occasions. They confirmed receipt of my request and promised to call me back, but that call never came. Subsequently, I was verbally informed that, "as per protocol," they did not issue refunds and that the money could be used as credit for other treatments, even though my contract includes reimbursement for services not provided within the specified timeframe. I was also told that expenses would be deducted, including an operating room reservation fee, but I am still waiting for a written breakdown and the corresponding receipts. Furthermore, the procedure was already scheduled, and pre-operative tests had been performed, yet I had not even had a consultation with the surgeon who was going to perform the operation. My main complaint is the lack of response, follow-up, and clarity in the process. To this day, I am still waiting for a formal response and the requested breakdown.

one_star_reviews.text:
We're regulars at this ice cream shop and come practically every week, often with my children. Because of this, we're quite familiar with the portion sizes they used to serve, and we can say that lately we've noticed a significant change: the scoops of ice cream are getting smaller and smaller.

Today, however, was the last straw. We ordered two scoops of ice cream, one pistachio and one hazelnut, and what they served us was so meager that the two scoops together looked like one. I politely told the girl that it seemed impossible that it was two scoops. The older woman explained that the girl was an apprentice, and I understood perfectly, so I told her it was fine and that she should just give me two properly portioned scoops.

I was surprised when she replied that she couldn't do that either because "they're not allowed to put more." So, honestly, I don't understand how you can charge for two scoops of ice cream and serve an amount that's practically enough for one.

It pains me to write this review because we've always come here and have been very happy until now. But when you're a regular customer and you see the portions decreasing, and then they tell you they can't give you a normal amount even though you're paying for it, it leaves you feeling very disappointed.

I hope they look into this, because if they keep reducing the portions so much, they'll end up losing the regular customers who have been coming for years.

One of the girls wasn't very nice. I ordered a hazelnut milkshake, and then when I asked for another one and a tub of ice cream, she gave me a dirty look and sent her colleague to serve me. The ice cream was very good.

Madrid Audio Review

My experience with Madrid Audio was very disappointing.

They agreed to install an exhaust sound system for me in a single day since I was coming from Barcelona. Despite telling me they could complete the job the same day without any problem, they finished much later than expected, and the result left much to be desired. When I picked up the vehicle, I noticed that the taillights were misaligned and that several interior and exterior parts of the vehicle, including the trunk, had scratches that weren't there before.

(The car is practically new.) Since it was already very late and they had to close up shop a while ago, and I had to get back to Barcelona, ​​they assured me that they would contact me first thing the next morning to resolve the issue. I could take the car to my trusted mechanic for repairs, and they would take care of it without any problem.

The next day, time passed, and no one contacted me first thing in the morning.
I had to contact them myself to try and resolve the issue. From that moment on, instead of taking responsibility or actively collaborating to clarify what happened, the attention I received has been insufficient and the problem handled very poorly. At the workshop, they told me they would take care of it without any problem, and once I was in Barcelona, ​​it was all excuses. They showed me photos of the vehicle with tools inside, trying to prove that the scratches were already there, when the vehicle was full of their tools from when they had already been working on it.
Since I had the system installed, I've experienced several Bluetooth and related errors that I honestly don't understand, but which I didn't have before they touched it. I've tried to resolve this situation amicably for a more than reasonable amount of time, but I haven't received a solution. I've even been forced to request a complaint form and initiate other actions to defend my rights as a consumer, and I'm still waiting for them to give me the complaint form. I cannot recommend this establishment based on my experience. A professional service isn't just about performing a correct installation, but also about responding when a problem arises. In my case, that response fell far short of what I consider acceptable. I traveled from Barcelona to Madrid to see them because they advertise heavily on Instagram, touting the high quality of their installation and professionalism, even though they're very expensive. I also couldn't find a workshop specializing in these types of speakers. But I finally decided to take on this huge expense because I wanted a top-notch installation in my car, and the installation was a complete failure. They even left the green tape protector they put on the sides visibly inside the speaker, which can't be removed without disassembling it again. It's pathetic... they really ripped me off!

⭐ If you have an enemy, recommend they buy here. Bravo!

I bought a new Peugeot 2008 for €24,500, with a maintenance contract and a five-year warranty. What I didn't know was that it also included a multisensory experience.

At 1,200 km, first visit to the garage. At 2,667 km, second breakdown and tow truck. Banging in the automatic gearbox (bang, bang, bang) and a barrage of warnings on the dashboard: ESP, ABS, "STOP", "engine stop"... A real spectacle! Too bad I didn't record the show.

The repair order lists "LACK OF POWER" and ABS and ESP warnings. I requested the diagnostic reports and error codes, but I still haven't received all the requested documentation.

Then came the complaints, the registered letter, and the intervention of the Consumer Protection Agency. Edauto informed me that the sales department would make me a buyback offer. In June, they told me it would be resolved in three days. It's the end of September, and I'm still waiting for that offer.

On September 30th, I went with my lawyer to a court-ordered mediation. The company's legal representative appeared, and no agreement was reached.

In short: a new car, breakdowns with less than 3,000 km, and months trying to get a solution.

A ten out of ten for special effects! As for the after-sales service, the phantom offer, and the customer service, I'd rather everyone draw their own conclusions.

My personal experience with Edauto. The story continues.

one_star_reviews.text:
We bought a synthetic wig from La Maison del Cabello in Alicante for over €700, precisely because, when we saw and tried it on, it looked very natural and we thought it was a good option for my mother in a situation that is already quite difficult.

I want to start by saying that, in our case, the initial service in the store was good. We liked the experience of entering a room and receiving personalized attention, and we felt well taken care of. That's precisely why we trusted the establishment and decided to make a purchase of this amount.

The problem came later. When we went to buy it, the pros and cons of a synthetic wig weren't clearly explained to us, especially regarding its tendency to tangle, mat, and deteriorate with use and friction. We knew it was synthetic and that it needed maintenance. In fact, we were told that it would need to be taken to the store approximately once a month for maintenance and that, over time, small "bumps" or tangles could appear, which they could fix themselves.

After only two days of use, and with very little wear time, the wig was already in terrible condition: there were areas that were very tangled and matted, to the point that you could barely move your fingers inside. The feel and appearance had also changed considerably compared to the day we bought it. For us, after having paid over €700, this was something we absolutely did not expect.

Today my mother went to the store to explain the situation. We suspected they probably wouldn't refund our money or necessarily replace the wig, but we expected, at the very least, understanding, empathy, and an explanation. However, the response was basically that "synthetic wigs are like that" and that they're used to seeing it.

These drawbacks were not explained to us before we bought it. If we had clearly understood how a synthetic wig could behave with use, we could have considered other options before spending over €700.

It's not about demanding that a synthetic wig behave like a natural hair wig. We fully understand that it has specific characteristics and requires particular care. The point is that, when making a purchase of this value, and especially when it's for someone going through a difficult time, we believe it's essential that both the advantages and disadvantages of the product are clearly explained so that everyone can make an informed decision.

Furthermore, when my mother came in today to explain that she no longer felt comfortable wearing it, we missed something as simple as, "We're sorry you're not happy; let's see what we can do to help." Instead, the response was quite blunt: "That's just how it is."

The way you treat and listen to the customer also matters, especially when dealing with such a sensitive situation.

We left with the feeling that the personalized attention we received initially didn't translate into consistent support when a problem arose. And, frankly, for the price we paid, we expected much more, both in terms of prior information about the product and in terms of the treatment and resolution of the problem afterwards.

I wanted to explain my experience with this company here, because in my opinion they are scammers and shameless. They sent me a hair extension, and three weeks after having it on my head, it started to frizz and swell so much that I had to wear it braided all day because it was impossible to wear it loose. I sent them photos, I even sent them the hair itself for them to examine, and their response was that it had probably been handled by another professional. To which I replied that the only professional was the girl who always puts in my extensions. I explained that I had only washed it with blue shampoo, but then I moisturized it thoroughly with the best hair masks on the market, the ones I always use. If hair is 100% natural, it can perfectly well be washed with blue shampoo, because I've been wearing extensions for years and I know what I'm talking about. They wouldn't even send me another new head of hair as compensation, saying they were very sorry but there was nothing they could do. So I want everyone to know, and I'm going to post these comments on every social media platform I can so people know what a bunch of crooks they are!

I'm giving it one star because I can't give it less. I decided to study the Higher Level Vocational Training Cycle in Marketing and Advertising at Eserp because of the center's prestige, but honestly, I couldn't regret the decision more. It was a complete waste of money.
During the program, I encountered a significant lack of professionalism, both from some of the teachers (though not all) and, above all, from the center's administration.
The most serious problem arose after completing the program. To gain university admission, we needed certain certificates, and instead of receiving help or clear information from the center, we had to figure out what to request and how to obtain it ourselves. Furthermore, we had to pay between €25 and €50 for a single document, which took about two weeks to arrive, right before the university's deadline.
I tried contacting the coordinator several times. When I called the office, they always told me he was in a meeting, couldn't speak to me, or that I should send an email. When I wrote to him, he often took a very long time to reply, and sometimes he didn't reply at all. This happened to everyone in my class.

After waiting two weeks for a document, I had to write directly to the director to get it. Oddly enough, the document arrived the next day, along with the corresponding apologies.

And as of today, September 23rd, I still haven't received the complete transcript I need to transfer my university credits.

It seems unbelievable to me that after paying what it costs to study here and having already finished the program, I have to chase the institution to get the documents I need to continue my studies.

My experience has been the complete opposite of what they advertise. If I could go back, I certainly wouldn't choose this place again.

Awful, a complete waste of money. The classes are incompetent, the paperwork takes forever and isn't done properly. Furthermore, the internship management is a disaster. Overall, a very bad experience; it's better to go to another center.

I identify myself as one of the people affected during the weekend of September 19-20. My initial intention was to put this incident behind me and avoid controversy, but after reading several reviews and responses and seeing that some accounts don't reflect our experience, I feel it's important to clarify.

On the 19th, we had booked the activity for 3:30 PM, as stated in the signed PDF, but due to a delay on the part of the company, it didn't start until 4:40 PM. We waited in the sun for approximately an hour.
For this activity, we were provided with old, worn, and even wet wetsuits. Furthermore, during the activity, the instructors capsized a boat and used the oars to push people in the water, causing them to sink. I believe these actions should be reviewed, especially for safety reasons.
Afterward, we had to wait for approximately an hour, soaking wet, while they collected the equipment. We were able to verify that another company didn't make its customers wait like that, and besides, their uniforms were impeccable.

I want to emphasize that our instructor, Javi, was very professional at all times, as was the employee who drove us back in the van. I thank them both for their excellent service.

The next day, five of us, not six, were unable to participate in the activity because we arrived 15 minutes late. We were waiting upstairs for the rest of the group because we didn't realize they were already changing. Given the situation, and the fact that we weren't allowed to participate for just 5 minutes more than the time allowed according to our signed agreement, we were the ones who called the Civil Guard because they were stalling on providing us with complaint forms. At no point were we asked to leave the premises. We spoke to the officers in a completely cordial manner, and they were able to hear the shouting and rude behavior the manager used towards me on the phone.

If there are security cameras, as has been claimed, they should be reviewed. The footage speaks for itself.

Finally, I want to clarify that it's true two people were absent on Saturday afternoon. Between the Saturday morning session, the Saturday afternoon session, and the Sunday morning group, we were a group of approximately 50 people.

I don't intend to stir up controversy. Simply put, after reading an account that I consider far removed from what actually happened, I believe those who read the reviews have the right to also hear the perspective of someone who was there and experienced the events firsthand.

Best regards.

Two people were missing from the activity, and because of the €40 shortfall, they wouldn't even let us pay afterward... it's like they're starving. My partner was there, and there were a lot of us... €100 at the very least... no lies here.

one_star_reviews.text:
We bought a car, the service was good and the overall experience was decent, but a problem arose. We called to resolve it, and they dragged their feet for what they claimed was a minor issue with the timing belt or some other problem.

Customer service is terrible; they don't know how to deal with customers or find solutions. They just read the problem and tell you to wait for the workshop's solution. And getting the car back is a nightmare. And you have to catch them in the mood to work, because... well, I don't recommend them. On top of that, we had to pay €0.50 per kilometer over the limit... but it took 12 days to get a refund.

This company is unprofessional and incompetent; most of the cars they sell are defective. My advice is not to buy a vehicle from them, as I and many other users (and there are quite a few of them) have the same or even worse experience than me. I can't understand how such a well-known company can sell defective vehicles and be so unprofessional. It's a disgrace.

Trial Period
My experience from the beginning has been quite disappointing. I recommend thoroughly inspecting the vehicle before accepting it, as there may be defects or damage that are not immediately apparent. I also advise against being swayed by the so-called trial period. In my case, I felt they were trying to get me to keep the vehicle at all costs, taking advantage of the €340 discount and the supposed 21-day trial.
Regarding the Premium Warranty, the information provided was scarce and opaque. They don't clearly explain exactly what it covers or which insurance company handles it, as the process seems to be done directly through the company itself. Furthermore, the vehicles are not sent to official dealerships, but to workshops they deem authorized.
My impression is that the covered repairs depend largely on their discretion, so I recommend carefully considering the purchase of a vehicle from this company. A quick look at the number of complaints and negative reviews confirms that this is a recurring concern among many customers. On the other hand, during service calls, the process has been slow and subject to continuous delays. The days the vehicle remains in the workshop are not always counted towards the warranty, and furthermore, the customer is responsible for transporting the car themselves, as they do not offer a collection service.
In short, my experience has been negative, and I believe it is important for future buyers to be aware of these aspects before making a decision.

I don't even know where to begin... but (I looked at a car on a Saturday at the beginning of September. By the 8th, I had everything for the car) NOW THEY DIDN'T CHECK ANYTHING, AND ON TOP OF THAT, THEY WERE INCAPABLE OF GETTING THE WIPERS FLUID OR WASHING IT. 400 km and engine problems, attempted theft... and the wipers were scratched and broken, things that weren't in the photo. When it came time to return the car, that's when the torture began... they don't know who's saying one thing and who's saying another, they don't know if it's Tuesday or Thursday... they tell you 5-7 days for returns... but they push the customer to their limit. They manage not to solve anything, and everyone passes the buck. For returns, they demand speed... but for paperwork, it's like a sales process. But when it comes down to it, they don't take care of the customer. You try to call to see where the refund is... and the customer service response is: "We've been talking for 30 minutes... what more do you want?! Excuse me, but fix the problem!!" I've already paid, and you don't even know when the refund has been processed... whether it'll be shipped one day, arrive another, or if it'll be delivered by DHL or the Three Wise Men...

I don't recommend buying anything here. They don't even inspect the cars. The process they handle with a Devil's is worse than getting a €20 refund on Amazon.

The returns department doesn't even answer emails anymore. Customer service doesn't want to know anything about it and makes excuses like the person in charge isn't available... or things like that.

Continuous problems with this company regarding their handling of the matter.

The car was supposed to have been serviced, but it didn't even have a battery, windshield washer fluid, or even a clean car. All of this is documented on Autohero's website for complaints.

Now, when it comes to getting the car... they're in a hurry. Without even seeing the car, they've already processed the exchange, told you what insurance they'll put on it, what day you can pick it up, and when you arrive, it has even more little issues... that aren't shown in the pictures. A complete disaster in terms of customer service, return procedures, management, and attitude. It's so rude you lose your temper because nobody can tell you exactly when you'll get your refund. But they have the car, they receive it, they know what they're doing... and providing terrible service is abysmal.

Find somewhere else to buy cars, because this place isn't worth it. It's too cheap and attractive, a cash scam.

I hope this helps other users avoid buying here... or at least have the car thoroughly inspected.

Disappointing experience.

Firstly, the entrance to the vehicle collection service is very poorly signposted, and there's a huge amount of red tape to deal with before even seeing a car.
As for the experience inside, the car left much to be desired. Although it looked decent on the outside (it was obvious inside that it had been in a rear-end collision, as it was covered in filler), the situation was quite different. When I opened the hood, I noticed the timing belt rattling and oil leaking from the engine. Furthermore, when I pulled the dipstick out, a lot of smoke came out. Finally, I'd like to emphasize that they presented the car as having been serviced and having the coolant at the minimum level, so it seems there hadn't been much of an inspection. An inexperienced person might be fooled, but it was a very unsatisfactory experience.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND BUYING FROM AUTOHERO.

I bought a beautiful Pomeranian as a gift and wanted to give it with all the necessary guarantees: veterinary care, vaccinations, a passport, and, of course, excellent insurance.

I signed up for Barkibu based on a recommendation, and my experience was fantastic. While I was the policyholder, I would have given it five stars without hesitation: the coverage seemed excellent for the price, it worked when I needed it, and I even recommended it to others.

The problem arose when I wanted to complete the gift and transfer the policy to the new owner's name. I filled out the corresponding form, and since then, I've been stuck in a kind of administrative limbo: I no longer have access to the app, and the new owner can't properly manage the insurance either.

The most frustrating thing is that the automated support can't handle a case that falls outside its usual workflow. And meanwhile, the payment obligation remains.

It's a shame because my overall assessment of the insurance product is still excellent. My dissatisfaction lies with how this issue has been handled and the inability to access human support capable of resolving it.

It does not seem reasonable to me to continue paying indefinitely for a service that, in the current administrative situation, I cannot use or manage, however premium it may be.
Price assessment
Great price

I requested reimbursement for my dog ​​Alan's veterinary expenses for a respiratory episode on September 24, 2026, and Barkibu rejected the invoice, claiming it was a "pre-existing condition." This is because my dog ​​had a bout of bronchitis on July 31, 2026, before the policy's start date of August 13, 2026, which has a 28-day waiting period for illnesses, ending around September 10. It's important to note that the report doesn't state that this episode was a continuation of the July bronchitis or that it was the same illness. The diagnosis was canine infectious tracheobronchitis with associated secondary rhinitis, meaning a subsequent infectious respiratory episode.

What I disagree with is the notion that a previous respiratory episode automatically implies that any subsequent respiratory problem is the same process or a pre-existing condition. Dogs, like people, can suffer from different respiratory infections or viruses at different times, and a history of a respiratory episode doesn't mean that any future episode will necessarily have the same origin, especially if the veterinary report doesn't confirm it.

Furthermore, I'm particularly concerned that Barkibu states in its resolution that this condition will also be excluded from future coverage, including any symptoms, injuries, or illnesses they deem related.
I understand that an insurance company has conditions and exclusions in its policy, but I believe that in this case, their interpretation is excessively broad and leaves the owner in a very vulnerable position. A previous respiratory episode shouldn't be automatically equated with any subsequent infectious respiratory episode without a veterinary report establishing that both processes are the same or that one stems from the other.
Before taking out insurance for my pet, I expected to have support when a veterinary problem arose. After this experience, I recommend carefully reading the exclusions and the company's interpretation of pre-existing conditions before signing a policy. My experience with Barkibu so far has been very disappointing.

⚠️ Be very careful with how Barkibu defines "pre-existing conditions," especially if you're insuring a puppy.

We took out an unlimited policy for our 3-month-old Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, who was insured with no pre-existing conditions. Two days after we got her, we went for her first puppy check-up and microchip verification. She was in good general health, and the vet simply noted that she had diarrhea the day before and soft stools that day. He didn't diagnose any gastrointestinal illness, and the episode resolved.
To our surprise, Barkibu later notified us that "diarrhea" had been classified as a pre-existing condition.
The worrying part is their own terms and conditions: they also consider a future illness to be pre-existing if it has "the same diagnosis or the same symptoms" as something that occurred before or during the waiting period, or if it is related to those symptoms.

This means that the problem isn't simply that they don't cover a consultation during the 28-day waiting period, which we completely understand. The problem is the risk that a common, transient, and undiagnosed symptom, such as a one-day bout of diarrhea during a puppy's adjustment period, could later be used to argue for coverage of a different illness that also causes diarrhea.

We have filed a formal complaint because we believe there is a huge difference between not covering an episode that occurred during the waiting period and turning that episode into a potentially permanent exclusion.

If you are considering taking out a Barkibu policy, don't just look at the reimbursement percentage or the 28-day waiting period. Read the definition of "Pre-existing Conditions" very carefully, especially the words "same symptoms." Any minor adjustment issue, even during the initial assessment, could be considered a pre-existing condition, which is very serious.

I will update this review when Barkibu responds formally and clarifies the actual scope they intend to give to this classification.

My experience with Inmolux has been frankly negative, exhausting, and very disappointing.

We started the purchase of a property with the genuine intention of closing the deal: we paid a deposit, had the property appraised, secured financing, and spent weeks trying to finalize the sale under reasonable terms for both parties.

During the process, we encountered management that, in our experience, was disorganized, unclear, and difficult to understand. The main problem arose with the terms of the deposit and the delivery deadlines for the property. Instead of reaching a balanced solution, we ended up being pressured to sign a deposit agreement whose terms did not offer the security we considered necessary in a transaction of this importance.

The situation escalated to the point that we had to hire and pay a lawyer to represent us and formally demand the return of the €2,000 deposit we had paid.

And, to this day, we still haven't recovered our money.

The most frustrating thing is that we weren't backing out of a purchase on a whim: we had the mortgage approved, the appraisal done, and the intention to buy. We simply wanted to do it with clear terms and the legal security that a sale of this amount should have.

The whole process has left us with a terrible feeling. Between managing the reservation, the proposed conditions, the deadlines, the appraisal, and ultimately having to resort to a lawyer to try to recover our own money, the experience has been disastrous.

My recommendation to any buyer is very simple: review absolutely all the documentation before handing over any money, get the reservation refund terms and delivery deadlines in writing, compare the appraisal price yourself, and if you have any doubts, consult a lawyer before signing.

What should have been the exciting purchase of a home has turned into a horrible experience, with lawyers involved, additional expenses, and €2,000 that we're still waiting to get back.

I repeatedly emphasized my interest in the property, stating that we want to view it and that everything is already arranged. I tried to offer options for viewing the apartment, but received no solution. Within 10 minutes, I received a message indicating it was reserved. Instead of making things so complicated and asking so many questions, get to the point. It seems you only offer housing to those who will then rent it out. Young people also want to live in their own city and in their own homes!

one_star_reviews.text:
Terrible customer service and total indifference
I just left the Tramas store in Ciudad Real (Saturday morning, October 3rd) and the experience was shameful. There were two sales assistants and neither showed the slightest interest in helping me.
I asked one of them for help to bring down a men's pajama set that was on the upper shelf, as I was looking for a small size. She said "one second" and completely ignored me, leaving me waiting indefinitely. I ended up having to try to bring the pajamas down myself (something that can be clearly seen on the security cameras).
To make matters worse, I approached the other sales assistant to ask about duvets and she also ignored my question. When I finally got fed up, I left and mentioned it to the cashier; her only response was a laughing "okay," without the slightest intention of apologizing or resolving the issue. I don't know if the distant and unpleasant treatment was due to some kind of prejudice or simply a complete lack of professionalism, but it's certainly regrettable that any customer is treated this way. In my case, I don't plan to return to the physical store; it's much more cost-effective to buy online than to waste time with staff who aren't interested in working.

When I started as a Production Technician, I had to relocate quickly from Guadalajara to Zaragoza, which involved moving and assuming all the expenses and commitments that came with the move. I was fully committed to the position and the company from the very beginning.

During the selection process and the various interviews, I wasn't informed of any specific physical requirements for the job.

From my first days on the job, I realized that my height (1.55 m) made the work difficult, as it involves handling radioactive material in a lead-lined chamber where it's necessary to reach and see certain areas to perform some tasks correctly. This difficulty was known and even mentioned by colleagues and supervisors. Although I reported the problem several times and suggested possible solutions, such as having a suitable support to reach and see the work areas correctly, no adjustments were made. Even so, I did everything I could to learn and adapt to the existing conditions.

My joining the company coincided with a period of high employee turnover, creating significant pressure to learn quickly. There were discrepancies between the tasks new employees were theoretically capable of performing and the practical tasks we needed to complete to learn the job properly. Direct supervision on the factory floor was limited, and much of the learning depended on my colleagues.

Another aspect I consider particularly important is the lack of feedback during my training period. During those months, I received no clear evaluation of my progress, nor was I given specific information about which aspects of my performance I needed to improve, which expectations I wasn't meeting, or if there was any risk of not passing the probationary period. Therefore, I didn't have the opportunity to know in advance if my performance was being considered insufficient or to correct any mistakes I might be making.

My relationship with the team was positive, and I believe I worked well with my colleagues. In fact, after I left, several colleagues stayed in touch, and one of them even helped me later to find new job opportunities. This contrasts with the possibility that there was an integration or attitude problem on my part.

What I consider particularly serious was the way the employment relationship ended. After having made the effort to relocate and commit to a position where I later discovered there was a significant physical challenge for me, I was summoned and told that I had not passed the probationary period, the reason given being that my learning was somewhat slower. All of this was done without any prior feedback that would have allowed me to understand this assessment and without any attempt to accommodate the difficulty I had reported.

The notification of my failure to pass the probationary period was delivered during a night shift, after I had gone to the plant specifically to continue my workday. The company is also located about 50 km from Zaragoza, so the commute was considerable. In my experience, the way the decision was communicated seemed insensitive, especially considering that I had not previously received clear feedback on my performance.

Furthermore, during my time in the role, operators could work up to two consecutive weeks on the night shift, which I personally found particularly demanding.

In short, I believe my experience reflects significant problems with planning, selection, prior information, onboarding, training, supervision, and communication.

A very, very bad experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
I made an appointment to inquire about psychological therapy, and it was one of the worst experiences I've ever had. First of all, I find it disrespectful how the women (I don't know if they were receptionists) kept coming into the room while I was supposedly being assessed. I say "supposed" because it doesn't seem normal for someone who is supposedly a psychologist to decide to comment on how they perceive me, as if it were a tarot reading. I was actually very lucky, because these kinds of things don't usually affect me much, but I find it shameful that this is the kind of attention someone who decides to ask for help might receive.

It's simply unacceptable that in a field as serious as mental health, what you get in an assessment is something like, "I think you are…," "I get the impression that what's happening to you…," among other incredibly unpleasant gestures like sighing while I was speaking, which suggests they were bored by what I was saying.

Furthermore, the woman who attended to me assumed I had difficulty expressing myself… when that's a quality I sorely lack. The problem with this is, what do you expect me to say when the space feels anything but safe? Interruptions, rudeness like sighing, unfounded assumptions about me… The truth is, the only impression I get is that this clinic is a scam, and it's shameful to play with people's mental health. That woman who attended to me wasn't a psychologist.
It's true I booked the appointment at very short notice, but if you don't have the necessary staff, just tell me no and I'll wait another day.
I felt like they were trying to sell me a beauty treatment instead of psychological therapy.
I'm very disappointed.

I saw information online about a visit to the Rubens exhibition and went specifically to attend.
I arrived at the museum and waited with the rest of the group for the tour to begin. Then Estrella Rodríguez approached me and, in front of everyone, told me that I couldn't participate because it was a private activity only for "Friends of the Museum."

I explained that I had found the information online. She replied that this couldn't be, that the information was private, and that she managed the website and social media herself. I insisted that I had arrived precisely because of that online post.
Since I had come alone, I asked if I could join the group. She rudely refused and told me there were no places available, even though the Rubens exhibition rooms were completely empty at that moment. I have also attached a photograph showing this.

I have also attached the online post and the printed program that was available at the museum, which lists the tour. I find it unacceptable that someone working in a public institution who interacts with the public should treat someone in this way when they are there in good faith to enjoy a cultural activity.

For this reason, I have already filed a formal complaint with the Museum of Fine Arts of Valencia, the Regional Ministry of Culture, and the Valencian Government.

I hope this type of behavior will be reviewed so that such actions do not tarnish the experience of visiting such a beautiful museum and enjoying such a valuable artistic heritage.

I went back to the back of the line and, as a result, I couldn't buy the chocolate I wanted. No one gave me a reasonable explanation as to when I'm supposed to be able to look at and buy those products, since they can't be seen from behind the line. I consider the way the cashier spoke to me completely inappropriate and unpleasant, especially given such a simple situation that could have been resolved perfectly well with courtesy and respect.

Almost two years have passed since then, and I still have the same unresolved problem. Furthermore, I don't even get a response to my WhatsApp messages. When I've tried to resolve it, the response has basically been to keep stalling and postponing the issue.

I understand that problems can occur in any workshop, but what I find unacceptable is that, once the problem has been reported and acknowledged, they refuse to take responsibility for effectively fixing it. The workshops also carry liability insurance for these types of situations.

After almost two years of waiting for a solution, my experience with this establishment has been very negative. I do not recommend the workshop because of the way they handled the problem and, above all, because of the lack of response and follow-up.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very negative experience with Arsan Windows.

We hired this company to supply and install a lift-and-slide window with a roller shutter, installed in March 2025.

The roller shutter box has a significant deformation in the front panel, which is particularly bent in the central area. Furthermore, we have observed that in this area the panel is not attached to the central frame with screws, adhesive, or any other fastening system. We believe there is a manufacturing and/or sizing defect that the company should review.

What has disappointed us most is the subsequent service from their salesperson, David. On July 28, 2025, we reported the problem via WhatsApp to their sales representative, David San Emeterio, and sent him a video showing the defect. More than a year has passed since then, and no technician has come to inspect it, nor have we received an effective solution.

In addition, the quote stated that we would receive a Warranty Certificate, a document we have not received. The quote also explicitly states "INCLUDING SCREW-INSTALLATION." The commitment to provide the warranty certificate is also explicitly stated in the document.

We have submitted another formal complaint requesting that they inspect the drawer and resolve the issue.

Our negative rating is primarily due to the lack of response and solution after we reported the problem in July 2025.

I will update this review if the company finally addresses the complaint and properly resolves the issue.

one_star_reviews.text:
Hi!

I wrote a review a few days ago, but it's nowhere to be found. I submitted it through JudgeMe after receiving an email asking me to rate my experience.
My shopping experience was pretty bad. Let me explain. I bought a backpack, a lunchbox, and a toy. In total, it cost over 70 euros to avoid shipping costs. The thing is, a few hours after the purchase, I changed my mind and wanted to exchange the backpack for a more expensive one. I called the store, and they said no problem, they would exchange the backpack, and I should send them a Bizum payment for the difference. I did so, and I immediately received an email confirming the cancellation of the first backpack and the new one.

But... the next day, the store called me and said that the person who helped me in the afternoon had made a mistake, and that the order had already been shipped when I called. So, I was going to receive the first backpack (the one I canceled) and not the second one (which I had already paid for). This person wasn't wrong; that's exactly what happened. I received what I wasn't expecting, the very thing they'd told me the previous afternoon was canceled.

Oh well, I thought, no big deal, they made a mistake and it'll be sorted out. The problem was that they didn't make it easy for me to exchange it. They kept telling me I had to pay the shipping costs. I told them the mistake wasn't mine, since they admitted the person who'd helped me that afternoon had made a mistake... Anyway, the next day I spent quite a bit of time talking to the store on WhatsApp, and "after they spoke with their legal team," as they told me, they offered to split the shipping costs. The thing is, by that point I was fed up with arguing, and I ended up keeping the product I didn't want, and waiting several days for the extra money I'd paid via Bizum.

That's why my experience was so bad, because I wasted so much energy on calls and WhatsApp messages over something that seemed much simpler.

I hope your purchase goes better and you receive a postcard like the one I received, wishing me a happy start to the school year. For that to happen, we need to be more willing to help when there's a problem like this.

one_star_reviews.text:
I've spent a considerable amount of time writing this review to try and be as objective as possible. However, in the end, all I can say about my experience with this garage is that it left me deeply disappointed, with a feeling of unprofessionalism and incompetence.

In March of last year, I took my Peugeot 3008, which until then had been well-maintained, to the garage as part of the MXL recall campaign for a timing belt replacement. From the start, they were very friendly and explained that it wasn't anything particularly serious and that they were used to performing this type of work.

After confirming that the part on my car was indeed damaged, they asked me to be patient and not to drive the vehicle while I waited for the part to arrive so they could carry out the replacement. I'll spare you the details of the waiting time and the lack of information I received during that entire period.

I finally got an appointment, left the car at the garage, and picked it up two days later. After driving barely 10 kilometers, the car suffered a breakdown that resulted in the engine seizing up.

That's when the real ordeal began. The garage wasn't responding to my insurance company's requests for an assessment. The garage, for its part, assured me they weren't responsible for the breakdown, but, "in their great generosity," they agreed to replace the engine, albeit with an estimate of over €8,000.

As a student, unable to pay such an amount, I decided to have the car moved elsewhere. A roadside assistance service came to pick it up, but called me to inform me that the vehicle wasn't ready. The most surprising thing is that I hadn't given any consent for the garage to work on the car again, since I had rejected the estimate.

It was then that I discovered, to my utter shock, that the car had been completely dismantled without my authorization. I found myself with a stripped vehicle, having not authorized any of these operations and without receiving a clear explanation of what they had done.

Faced with this situation, I even wondered if they had dismantled the car to try and hide their incompetence.

Two months later, I finally got my car back. You can imagine my surprise when I found boxes full of disassembled parts, when, once again, I hadn't given any consent for them to dismantle anything at all.
After trying numerous times to get explanations and answers, the garage decided to stop responding. Finally, I had no other option but to abandon my efforts.

In short, this experience has cost me a car in which I had invested a lot of money, and as a student, it has cost me over €1,000 in towing and transport fees.

My advice is very simple: be very careful before entrusting your vehicle to this garage. In my case, the experience has been extremely costly and frustrating, and the level of communication and consideration for the customer has been, from my point of view, completely inadequate.

After everything that happened, I deeply regret having trusted this establishment. Fortunately, there are many other professional and competent workshops.

one_star_reviews.text:
Total disappointment. They make their living by scamming people out of reservation deposits. Don't trust their word because they're liars who offer no solutions, and they're incredibly rude when they see you won't give in. The case was handled by Daniel Lucía at the Autoback dealership in the Navalcarnero industrial park.

I requested a refund of my reservation.
On April 21st, I made a reservation for a Peugeot 308. Later, on the 25th, I went to their dealership to see it, and that same day, they told me the reservation would be changed to a Kia Ceed (a reservation that was never actually made). I expressed interest in the Kia, but made it clear that I would discuss it at home and then communicate my decision.

On the 26th, I confirmed my interest in buying the Kia, indicating that, in principle, I would take it, but always conditional on taking a test drive before making a final decision. I never confirmed the purchase.

It was then mentioned that, due to work commitments and coinciding with a long weekend, the vehicle test drive would take place on the 4th, outside the cancellation period that had been discussed. For this reason, on the 27th, I insisted on a refund of the deposit to avoid losing it within the refund period. At that time, Daniel told me that I wouldn't lose the deposit, that I shouldn't worry, and that the purchase paperwork should be prepared, even after I explained again that my final decision depended on taking the test drive. I never stated that it was final.

On the 30th, I finally informed them that I couldn't proceed with the transaction and again insisted on a refund, since I had been told I wouldn't lose it. In response, I was told that the deposit would not be refunded.

I want to reiterate that the deposit was never modified and there was never a final and binding acceptance of the purchase, as it was conditional upon taking the test drive, a condition that was communicated at all times. I followed up later, since I was told I would get a response after I expressed my disagreement. I had to call again myself, and they told me to send an email because he wasn't going to do anything about it, even though he was rude and raised his voice.

I sent the email as instructed, months have passed, and I still haven't received a response.

I'm not going to get my money back, but I hope this can at least help someone else avoid the same thing. Don't trust his word; he doesn't care about the customer, he only cares about the money, and if they have to lie, they'll do it without remorse to keep what isn't theirs.

I find it appalling that someone buys a vehicle there, and after six months the engine fails, the battery dies, and when they ask for a solution, the customer has to go to another garage to get an estimate to send it to for evaluation and then see if they accept it or not. You're supposed to be the ones selling and providing the warranty, so the car should come into your workshop and you should carry out the necessary repairs so the customer is satisfied. People buy a car to avoid expenses for a reasonable amount of time. And when it comes to honoring the warranty, you just keep stalling.

I've been a Nespresso customer for almost 10 years. There have been many pleasant moments during this time, but after reading some reviews, I was surprised to discover that other customers are offered different coffee options or alternatives by store employees. I've never been offered anything like that.

I've always encountered rather cold and distant service, and I feel like customer service has been getting worse over the years.

But the most unpleasant experience was my latest online order. They simply didn't deliver it. The last message I received said, "You will receive your order today." And then, nothing.
I haven't received a refund, nor have I received any message with an explanation or even an apology. In my opinion, the company is responsible for choosing the delivery company, and if the order has been lost, they should resolve the issue and send me my order or refund my money.
After almost 10 years as a customer, I find it especially disappointing to encounter such indifference towards regular customers. A complete letdown.
